Rule made returnable forthwith and heard finally with the consent of learned Advocates for the parties.

2. By this Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the Petitioners are seeking a declaration about lapsing of reservation under Section 127 (1) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 (for short 'MRTP Act') and consequently a writ of mandamus, directing the Respondents to issue a notification under sub-section (2) of Section 127 of the MRTP Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Admitted facts are that, the land of the Petitioners' bearing Survey No.438/2/A was reserved for School and Play Ground in the Development Plan of the year 1976.
Thereafter in the year 1989 the Petitioners' land was again reserved for High School and Play Ground.
Even in the Development Plan of 2016, the Petitioners' land was again shown as reserved for High School and Play Ground.
Pursuant to the order of this Court dated 10 th July, 2019 in Writ Petition No.1732 of 2018, a portion of 46 R land out of Survey No.438/2/A was de-
reserved.
In addition to that, 35.5 R portion out of Survey No.438/2/A was deserved by notification dated 24.08.2015 under Section 127 (2) of the MRTP Act.
The remaining portion of 11.5 R, which is subject matter of present Writ Petition was not covered by the said notification.
5. Petitioners issued notice dated 30/11/2012 to the Respondent - Municipal Council under Section 127 of the MRTP Act.

Respondent - Municipal Council has not initiated acquisition proceedings under old Land Acquisition Act or under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 2013')

sentences.text: 6. Mr. Mukul Kulkarni, learned Advocate for Petitioners would submit that the property of the Petitioners was reserved in the Development Plan of 1976 as well as 1989 by Respondent No.4 - Municipal Council and despite the same, no steps for acquisition have been initiated at any point of time.

He relied upon the Judgment in Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Co. Ltd Vs. The State of Maharashtra reported in (2015) 11 SCC 554 and submitted that the re-reservation of wp-6489-2023 the land in the successive Development Plans is not permissible and on that ground the re-reservation of the land of the Petitioners' in the Development Plan of 2016 deserves to be quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Co. Ltd Vs. The State of Maharashtra reported in (2015) 11 SCC 554
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would further submit that the land of the Petitioners' cannot be kept under reservation in perpetuity, as their right of ownership would otherwise be defeated.
7. Mr. D. B. Thoke, learned Advocate for Respondent No.4 - Municipal Council would submit that the Respondent - Municipal Council does not run any High School, but runs a Primary School.

He would further submit that, therefore, a request was made that reservation for Municipal High School should not be included in the Development Plan, however, if the reservation of the playground is continued, it would benefit the people of that vicinity.
He fairly submitted that,
Municipal Council does not have necessary funds for acquiring the Petitioners' subject land.
8. We have considered the rival submissions and perused the papers.
It is evident from the record that subject property of the Petitioners is kept under reservation for the last 47 years.

In view of de-reservation of the portion of land out of Survey No.438/2/A and further portion of 35.5 R by notification under Section 127 (2) of MRTP Act dated 24.08.2015, the continuation of reservation of the subject property of wp-6489-2023 the Petitioners for indefinite period is arbitrary and the same cannot be sustained.
9. Admittedly, no steps for acquisition were taken pursuant to the notice dated 20.11.2012 issued under Section 127 of the MRTP Act.

10. The subject property is again reserved for High School and Play Ground and Respondent No.4 - Municipal Council does not operate any High School since last about 50 years and has accordingly informed Respondent No.1.
In spite of that, action of Respondent No.1 in reserving the subject property for High School is vitiated by non- application of mind.

Taking into consideration the statement made by the Municipal Council that they do not require subject property for High School and that they do not have necessary funds to acquire the subject property for play ground, there is no propriety in continuing reservation of the subject property.
11. The Issue raised in present Petition is covered by the decision of this Court in Writ Petition No.4963 of 2016 decided on 04.12.2025.
12. For the aforestated reasons, the Writ Petition is allowed.

13. It is declared that the reservation at Serial No.22 in the wp-6489-2023 Development Plan dated 06.04.2016 of Respondent No.4 - Municipal Council, in respect of Petitioners' land bearing Survey Laxmibai Vishnu Patil Since Deceased ... vs The State Of Maharashtra Through Its ... on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153293544/
3 No.438/2/B to the extent of 11.5 R situated at Chalisgaon, Dist. Jalgaon, has lapsed.

14. The Respondents shall take immediate steps and shall issue a notification under sub-section (2)
of Section 127 of the MRTP Act, in any case within 12 (twelve) weeks from today.
15.
No order as to costs.
16. Rule is made absolute in the above terms.
